notes_list.title: Pyridine — Basicity and Electrophilic/Nucleophilic Reactivity
notes_list.basic_overview: Pyridine is an aromatic six-membered heterocycle whose nitrogen lone pair lies outside the aromatic sextet, allowing protonation without destroying the aromatic π system.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Pyridine is more basic than pyrrole but less basic than many aliphatic amines. The ring is deactivated toward EAS and activated at certain positions toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution depending substituents.
notes_list.examples: Pyridine + H+ → pyridinium. N-oxide formation alters ring electronics and can change substitution patterns.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Acid-base chemistry occurs readily in protic media; EAS often requires forcing conditions.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Protonation occurs at nitrogen using its nonaromatic lone pair. EAS must attack an electron-poor ring and is therefore difficult; nucleophilic attack can be facilitated at 2/4 positions under suitable substitution.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Basicity is an equilibrium property and depends on solvent. Nucleophilic substitution has its own kinetic controls.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not count the nitrogen lone pair as one of the six aromatic π electrons.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
